First-touch grading (triage seat, session `session_014tGY3fzu4uwCoe7HrfUtWg`): **promoted to `pm:queue`, type Task, narrow scope.**

Scope graded IN: convert `managed-extension-fields.test.ts:281` to the package's established `findUp` idiom, lower the `@objectstack/plugin-auth` TEST_DEBT entry (re-measure the number at the landing ref — the card's own warning), and rewrite the entry's composition `note` in the same edit. Worth its size because the wrong spelling sits in the file agents are pointed at as the pattern to copy.

Scope graded OUT (the triage call the filer requested): the sibling `tsconfig.test.json` graduation. Retiring the whole class is attractive but it converts a one-line cleanup into a wholesale test-layer type-check program interacting with a 111-entry debt ledger — that is its own card with its own pricing if anyone wants it, not a rider here.

Size/model suggestion: S, sonnet — mechanical, gate-adjudicated (the ledger ratchet itself proves the change).

Justification below: the card's target number is already stale, and the ledger file contains a self-test fixture that looks exactly like the thing being edited. Both are judgment traps, not mechanics.
- **Clause-②: no** — test-seed idiom swap plus a shrink-only ledger decrement. No contract accept/reject change, no public surface widening. Tier read live from `dispatch-gates.mjs` (`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER = 'claude-fable-5'`, line 1927), not invoked.
- **Serial**: dispatched ALONE on `plugin-auth/**`. #9653/PR #10013 merged at `e717ba111` (landing content-verified), which released the lock; **#9941 stays queued behind this card** and will not be dispatched until this one lands — this is the card that moves the TEST_DEBT number, and two concurrent plugin-auth cards is exactly the ledger collision the seat has been holding the queue against.

**Premise re-verified on `origin/main@e717ba111` — and it has drifted since the card was written:**

- ⚠️ **The recorded ledger number is `110`, not the `111` this card prescribes.** `check-type-check-coverage.mjs:732` reads `errors: 110`. The card's own warning ("re-measure at the ref the PR lands on, not at the ref it was written on") has **materialized** — PR #10013 re-measured this same entry at 110 hours ago. So the card's instruction "lower 111 → 110" is stale on its face; the work is still real, but the target number must be **measured, never copied from the card**.
- The defect itself is intact: `managed-extension-fields.test.ts:281` still reads `const HERE = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));`, with the `fileURLToPath` import at line 104. Counter-check applied (the file returns 30 hits for its own `describe`/`it(` spellings, so the search is live).
- The idiom to copy is intact at `member-role-canonical.test.ts:65-80` — a `findUp` walk keyed on the package manifest's `name === '@objectstack/plugin-auth'`, with the CJS/TS1470 rationale written out at `:62-63`.

⚠️ **Trap flagged for the dev — do not "fix" it**: `check-type-check-coverage.mjs:2752` contains `{ ledger: 'TEST_DEBT', name: 'plugin-auth', recorded: 111, actual: 112 }`. That is a **self-test fixture** for the #8435 ratchet-offer detector, not the ledger. It must stay exactly as it is. Editing it because it "still says 111" would silently break a convention check that otherwise passes vacuously.

Scope, per triage: convert the seed to the `findUp` idiom, lower the ledger entry to the **re-measured** number, and rewrite the entry's composition `note` in the same edit — its tally (`TS2493 x42, TS18048 x24, …`) already describes a state that predates 111 and says so; it must not be left describing a tally that no longer holds. ⛔ **Graded OUT**: the sibling `tsconfig.test.json` graduation. Retiring the whole class is attractive and is its own card with its own pricing — ⛔ not a rider here.

Named gate families to re-derive against the real diff; `check:type-check-coverage` is the adjudicating gate and its own verdict line is the proof this card is done.

**ACCEPT** — PR #10028, head `1252262be`. **Deviation adjudicated: Option A, as shipped.**

## The deviation, and why the dev was right and my dispatch was wrong

The card, the triage comment, and **my dispatch** all prescribed the package's `findUp` idiom. All three were written without knowing that `check:cross-package-test-inputs` recognises **exactly two** directory seeds — `dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))` and `__dirname` — when it statically detects that a test escapes its package.

The dev didn't take that on faith or quietly substitute something; it **measured the counterfactual**. Ablation leg 1 applied the prescribed `findUp` shape and captured the gate's own words:

> `- @objectstack/plugin-auth declares a cross-package input radius, but no test in it reads outside the package any more. Delete the entry (and its turbo.json inputs)` — exit 1

And `managed-extension-fields.test.ts` is the **only** escaping read that gate can see in `plugin-auth`, so it alone holds the package's declared radius (`packages/**/*.object.ts`) and the matching `turbo.json#test` inputs. Following my instruction literally would have forced one of two bad outcomes: a red gate, or deleting the entry and putting this repo-wide `*.object.ts` sweep back into #7802's blind spot — turbo replaying a cached green for a diff that changed another package's object file.

`const HERE = __dirname;` satisfies **both** constraints at once: TS1470-free under this CJS-typed package, and detector-recognised. And it is not an invention — `packages/platform-objects/src/managed-api-method-affordance-sweep.test.ts:95-113` had already reasoned its way there for the structurally identical repo-wide walk, for these same two reasons. My dispatch said "match the existing idiom rather than inventing a variant"; the dev matched the *right* existing idiom, which is a better reading of that instruction than the one I had in mind.

Options B and C correctly rejected: B (teach the detector the `findUp` shape) is outside the declared surface and repo-wide in effect — its own card; C (delete the entry) is measurably harmful.

## Verified against the diff

- **The number was measured, not copied — from anywhere.** The dev reproduced `check-type-check-coverage.mjs`'s own `measureTestDebt()` (same generated project, exclusion lifted, paths absolutised, typeRoots reconstructed, same `tsc --noEmit --pretty false`, same counter). **BEFORE = 110, matching the recorded value** — which is what validates the reproduction rather than just asserting it — and **AFTER = 109**, TS1470 gone with no other diagnostic moved. Ledger `110 → 109`. The card's `111` was never used.
- **The adjudicating gate's load-bearing line is quoted**: `surplus: none — every entry sits exactly at its measurement, so any new error is red.` Leaving 110 would have printed a `can be lowered` line instead. That is the difference between "green" and "correct".
- **The note was re-tallied from the same run, not rescaled** — and the dev explains why a rescale was impossible: the old tally was taken at 131 and named `TS2740 x19` / `TS2741 x8`, but **TS2740 has gone to zero outright** and TS2741 is 3. It also now records the `111 → 110` move PR #10013 made without touching the note, which is precisely how a composition written at 131 ended up sitting over an entry reading 110. That is the #7038 shape being closed, not papered over.
- **The self-test fixture is untouched** — it does not appear in the diff. The trap held.
- **Unused `dirname`/`fileURLToPath` imports removed** (`noUnusedLocals` is on).
- **Two ablations, each predicted before running, each restored byte-identically** (`git hash-object 9c57a17d7b…` before and after both, tree clean). Leg 2 is the one I asked for: seed the scan at a wrong directory and the file goes red — observed `AssertionError: expected 0 to be greater than 15` plus an ENOENT on the auth-manager read. That is **positive proof `HERE` still resolves where it did**, which is the real risk of this change; the type error was never the risk. The no-rebuild statement is given *with its reasoning* (pure source scan on one leg, vitest-from-source on the other, no `dist/` on either resolution path) rather than asserted.
- `plugin-auth` 57 files / 1301 tests pass; typecheck exit 0 with `> tsc --noEmit` echoed rather than a zero-match false green; the full gate union quoted by verdict line; exit codes captured before any pipe.
- `skip-changeset` applied **and read back**. Correct: one test file plus one CI-internal gate script, publishing nothing.

## The finding this turned up is the more valuable half

**#10029**: `rate-limit-storage-isolation.test.ts` reads `packages/runtime/src` and `packages/services/service-sms/src` through a `findUp` seed the gate **cannot see**, so neither directory is in `plugin-auth`'s declared globs or its `turbo.json#test` inputs — a live #7802 blind spot, currently **masked** because a different file in the same package escapes visibly and keeps the entry reading as live. Note the consequence: if anyone later "modernises" `managed-extension-fields.test.ts` to `findUp` — exactly what this card told them to do — the mask drops and the radius silently goes stale. The code comment now shipped in that file says so in place, which is the right defence.

On the graded-OUT `tsconfig.test.json` graduation: keeping it out, as triage set it. Recorded from this round, though: the two constraints on this file's seed are **independent** (tsc module semantics vs. a source-scanning gate's recognised spellings), and only the ESM route dissolves the tension rather than threading it. Not a reason to widen this card.

Landing plan: gate families read by name; flip ready + enqueue on `completed: success`. Once this lands, `plugin-auth/**` is free and #9941 is next.
